```{r setup, include=FALSE}

```

H1: Those who report a history of infidelity (categorical) will report lower relationship satisfaction/commitment (composite).

H2: Willingness to marry without love will be negatively correlated with age.


## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)


#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("data/raw/data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows. Will give number of rows and number of columns. 
#In this case 117294 participants, 273 variables
dim(raw)
head(raw[,c("ResponseId")])
str(raw) #tells you amount of observations and variables, and also variables and first values


#make data with ID, age, history of infidelity, willingness to marry without love, and relationship satisfaction/commitment prqc 1-6 unchanged
#Go to codebook to find variable names for this dataset
data <- data_doctored[,c("ResponseId",
                         "Age",
                         "infidelity",
                         "Love_would_you_marry_1",
                         "prqc_1",
                         "prqc_2",
                         "prqc_3",
                         "prqc_4",
                         "prqc_5",
                         "prqc_6")]

#This should now show less variables than before (10) in this case
dim(data)
str(data) #now is more trackable, because it only has the columns we need






```


## 2. Check participant IDs
We want to validate the participant ID, because eg. there can be duplicates (two responses from one participant), or no data at all for a participant 

```{r participant_ids}

#count na. #False is 0, True is 1 --> It will count how many "true" values aka. NA data are there 
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank. (na.rm will remove those that are NA and just leave those that are blank)
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)

#count duplicates. (How many not unique IDs are there)
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#All these previous can be found out with: 
summary(data$Response_Id)

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs. Tells you which one is the NA Participant Id in the order of columns.
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
missingID
data[missingID,]
print(data[missingID,]) #we remove row because the particpant has only Nas


#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),] #! is saying "no"/ It will only leave the things that are not NA
dim(data) #should now display one less participant
```


## 3. Recode Infidelity

```{r infidelity}
# codebook: 0 = No infidelity, 1 = Infidelity
table(data$infidelity, useNA="ifany")
#turn infidelity into a factor with labels No infidelity and Infidelity

data$infidelity <- factor(data$infidelity,
                         levels=c(0,1),
                         labels=c("No Infidelity","Infidelity"))
                         
table(data$infidelity,useNA="ifany")


```
## Make composite relationship satisfaction and committment

```{r Relationship satisfaction and committment}
#make relData for respondents committed and satisfied in relationship

table(data$prqc_1, useNA ="ifany")
relData <- data[data$prqc_1 %in% c(1,2,3),] #keeps only 1,2,3 as rows
  #compare before to now by typing dim(data) and compare to dim(relData) (in console)


#define the items to check; all four use response codes 1-7
#prqc_1-6: 1=Not at all, 7=Extremely
likert7 <- c("prqc_1","prqc_2","prqc_3","prqc_4","prqc_5", "prqc_6")


#check the summaries and missing responses
summary(relData[,likert7])
  #looks good because all max values are 7
colSums(is.na(relData[,likert7])) #provides number of NAs for each item 

#inspect the response frequencies for each item #to get an idea of how people responded
#for each item in likert7
for(i in likert7) {
  print(i)
  print(table(relData[,i],useNA="ifany"))
}

  

#replace any codes outside 1-7 with NA
for(i in likert7) {
  relData[,i] <- ifelse(relData[,i] %in% 1:7, relData[,i],NA) #testing whether value in column of real data is it a number from 1:7
}


```

## 6. Calculate satisfaction/commitment
Make a composite score 
### Some need reverse coding, some need to averaged/summed/weighted --> all details are in the codebook!

```{r satisfaction/commitment}
#group commitment variables (prqc_1, prqc_2, and prqc_3, prqc_4, prqc_5, and prqc_6) #average these values
#these ask how committed, dedicated, and devoted respondents are
#none requires reverse coding
romVars <- c("prqc_1", "prqc_2", "prqc_3","prqc_4", "prqc_5", "prqc_6") #grouped commitement variables


#calculate relationship data (reldata)m satisfaction/commitment as the mean of all 6 items
#for NAs, conduct available item mean
relData$romsatisfaction_commitment <- rowMeans(relData[,romVars], na.rm=TRUE) 
  #pick only commitment variables and averaging all the values per row 

#check the score
summary(relData$romsatisfaction_commitment)

#make h1Data with ID, infidelity and prqc
#store this into a new data set
h1Data <- data[,c("ResponseId",
                  "infidelity",
                  "relData")]
#HAVING ISSUES HERE
#make h2Data with ID, age, and willingness to marry without love
#keep participants with both qoa and commitment present
#do not apply the H1 preference filter to this hypothesis
h1Data <- relData[!is.na(relData$qoa)&!is.na(relData$commitment), 
                  c("ResponseId", "qoa", "commitement")]
need to combine these two
```


HYPOTHESIS 2: Willingness to marry without love will be negatively correlated with age
## 5. age & willingness to marry without love
```{r hypothesis 2}
#make h2Data with ID, age, and willingness to marry without love
#keep participants with both qoa and commitment present
#do not apply the H1 preference filter to this hypothesis
h2Data <- data[,c("ResponseId",
                  "Age",
                  "Love_would_you_marry_1")]
```

## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$preference_imp_physat)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 1-7
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$qoa)
range(h2Data$commitment)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Age",
  "Love_would_you_marry_1")

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "infidelity",
  "Relationship satisfaction/commitment: mean of available prqc_4-6 responses, each 1=Not at all to 7=Extremely; need to check reverse coding; at least one valid response required"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid sex-at-birth category, and six
allocations between 0 and 30 that total 30. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, relationship status 1, 2, or 3, and
valid nonmissing qoa and at least one valid commitment response.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
